newsitem.title: USA: San Diego wins court ruling in Calif. welfare case.
newsitem.headline: San Diego wins court ruling in Calif. welfare case.

text.p: California's Supreme Court ruled on Monday that San Diego County may receive repayment for certain welfare costs in a decision that could open the door for other counties to seek reimbursements, attorneys involved in the case said.
In an opinion released in San Francisco, the state Supreme Court remanded to the state's Commission on State Mandates "to determine the amount of reimbursement, if any, due San Diego."
San Diego was seeking reimbursement from the state for certain costs of providing health-care services to the poor.
Attorneys for San Diego County hailed the ruling but said the county's fight for reimbursement was far from over.
"The check is not in the mail because we now essentially have to prove our damages," said Ian Fan, deputy San Diego County counsel. "It will be a while before we get any money."
Fan added, however, that the state Supreme Court ruling could clear the way for other counties to obtain repayment.
"It sets a new standard for what a mandate is, and that will be important for all other counties in the state," he said.

In its ruling on Monday, the state's Supreme Court affirmed "the finding that the Legislature's exclusion of medically indigent adults from Medi-Cal (the California Medical Assistance Program) 'mandate(d) a new program or higher level of service.'"
California state officials said they have to review the ruling further before commenting in detail, though they warned the decision could have serious financial implications.

"This ruling could open up a number of significant fiscal and policy issues," said H.D. Palmer, a spokesman for the state's Department of Finance. "But we're not going to make a snap judgement on dealing with this."
